chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Fudayl ibn Sukkarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام): “May I be sacrificed for you, if you see fit to teach me: did Allah, majestic is His Face, know before He created the creation that He is One? For your followers have differed. Some of them said: He had known before He created anything from His creation. And some of them said: the meaning of ‘He knows’ is ‘He does’; so today He knows that there is no other than Him before the bringing about of things.”
So they said: “If we affirm that He never ceased being knowing that there is no other than Him, then we have affirmed along with Him something other than Him in His eternality.”
So if you see fit, O my master, teach me that which I will not go beyond to anything else.” Then he (عليه السلام) wrote: “Allah has never ceased being Knowing. Blessed and Exalted is His mention.”

key_terms.أَزَلِيَّتِهِ: His eternality; the state of having no beginning
key_terms.الْخَلْقَ: the creation; all created beings and things
key_terms.عَالِمًا: Knowing; describing Allah as eternally possessing knowledge
key_terms.مَوَالِيكَ: your followers/allies; those attached in wilayah to the Imam
key_terms.يَعْلَمُ: to know; here, referring to Allah’s attribute of knowledge

ai.seo_question: Did Allah know before creating creation that He is One?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a theological question about Allah’s eternal knowledge before the creation of all things. Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) gives a concise creedal answer, affirming that Allah has always been Knowing, thereby establishing divine knowledge as an eternal attribute.
